How to Submit Public Comment

Members of the Public who wish to submit public comment may do so using one of
the following methods. Public comment is limited to the time allotted.

In-Person: Complete a Speaker Card, indicating the agenda item number and submit
it to the City Clerk prior to the meeting. Speakers shall be limited to three (3) minutes
per person per item. At the Mayor’s discretion, the time limit may be shortened to allow
all speakers to address the City Council. Please note that interactions between the City
Council, City staff, and the public during meetings are subject to the City’s Rules of
Decorum.

Website: Electronic submission of Public Comment is available via the online public
comment form at Public Comment. Public Comment submitted electronically by 4:00
P.M. on the meeting day will be forwarded to the City Council before the meeting for
their consideration, but will not be read during the meeting. Comments submitted after
4:00 P.M. will be forwarded to Council but may not be received before the meeting.

  C. CASH AND INVESTMENT REPORT – JULY 2025

  In accordance with the City of San Gabriel’s 2025-2026 Adopted Investment
  Policy (Resolution No. 25-25) and California Government Code Section 53646,
  the Finance Director is to render an investment report to the City Council, City
  Treasurer, City Manager, and the City Attorney. The Cash and Investment
  Report is presented to receive and file in accordance with the City’s adopted
  2025-2026 Investment Policy.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council receive and file the Cash and
  Investment Report for July 2025.

  D. RESOLUTION NOS. 25-32 AND 25-33 SETTING THE RATE AND AMOUNT
  NECESSARY FOR THE 2025-2026 FISCAL YEAR RETIREMENT LEVY

  The City’s retirement costs are funded by a special property tax levy authorized
  by the voters in 1948, which requires the City Council to annually establish a tax
  rate to pay for the state employees’ retirement system cost. Based on the
  assessed valuation ($7,494,322,933 – an increase of 4.6% over Fiscal Year 2024-
  2025 value) prepared by the Auditor Controller and the recommended
  continued levy of 14 cents per $100 of assessed property value, the amount to
  be generated is estimated at $10,492,052 for Fiscal Year 2025-2026. Based on
  the Fiscal Year 2025-26 budget, the Retirement Fund is projected to result in a
  deficit of about $1.3 million, as retirement costs of $11,970,267 for Fiscal Year
  2025-2026 will exceed the combined total of the current retirement fund
  balance and the retirement tax levy. This shortfall will require temporary
  borrowing from other funds until the retirement tax revenue is sufficient to
  cover the retirement cost.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – August 19, 2025  3
   California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 25-32, setting the
  tax rate at 14 cents per $100 assessed valuation, and Resolution No. 25-33,
  fixing the amount of property taxes to be generated for the City’s employees’
  retirement cost for Fiscal Year 2025-2026.

  E. PURCHASE OF VIDEO DETECTION CAMERA SYSTEMS FOR TRAFFIC-
  SIGNALIZED INTERSECTIONS FROM ITERIS, INC. FOR $724,011.75,
  INCLUDING A 10% CONTINGENCY, USING MEASURE R FUNDING

  The Public Works Department proposes to procure 142 new video detection
  camera systems to be installed at 36 traffic-signalized intersections citywide,
  enhancing the efficiency and effectiveness of traffic signal maintenance
  operations. Measure R funds will be used and will be reimbursed by Metro in
  accordance with their quarterly application deadlines and review processes. No
  General Funds will be used for this purchase. Funds are now available in the
  Fiscal Year 2025-2026 approved budget. The cost for the purchase order
  issuance for cameras procurement is $658,192.50 plus a 10% contingency of
  $65,819.25.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: This project is
  determined to be Categorical Exempt per CEQA Section 15301 – the project
  consists of minor alterations to existing public right of way facilities. No potential
  for significant impacts to the environment are anticipated in this project.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council award the bid and approve the
  purchase of video detection camera systems from Iteris, Inc., and authorize the
  City Manager to execute a purchase order with Iteris, Inc. in the amount of
  $724,011.75, which includes a 10% contingency.

  F. SAN GABRIEL HISTORICAL ASSOCIATION FEE WAIVER REQUEST FOR USE
  OF GRAPEVINE ARBOR FOR FUNDRAISER EVENT

  The San Gabriel Historical Association (SGHA) is requesting a fee waiver to
  utilize the Grapevine Arbor for a fundraising event on September 4, 2025. As a
  volunteer-driven, non-profit organization, the SGHA depends on the success of
  this event to fund the preservation, maintenance, and hospitality of the

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – August 19, 2025  4
   Museum and Hayes House. The SGHA is requesting a waiver of the rental fee
  as an expression of support for the SGHA’s contributions to San Gabriel’s
  history and culture. If approved, this item would authorize a $530 rental fee
  waiver for Fiscal Year 2025-2026.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council waive the facility rental fee in the
  amount of $530.

  G. THEATRE FEE WAIVER REQUEST BY UNITED CHARITY FOUNDATION FOR
  CHILDREN’S HOLIDAY PROGRAM

  The United Charity Foundation has requested a waiver of rental fees for their
  upcoming community Children’s Holiday Program, scheduled to take place on
  November 29, 2025 at the San Gabriel Mission Playhouse. The request is for a
  $4,775 waiver of Facility Rental, Equipment Usage and Administrative fees,
  reducing their rental cost to $3,323. Staff recommends a waiver of facility rental
  and equipment usage costs of $4,025, but not the administrative fees. The
  current rental subsidy account has sufficient funds to cover the recommended
  rental waiver of $4,025. However, should the usual request for fee waivers come
  in throughout the year, a budget adjustment will likely need to be requested if
  the waivers are approved.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council grant a waiver of the United Charity
  Foundation event fee in the amount of $4,025 for the November 29, 2025
  Children’s Holiday Program.

  H. DONATION OF 2002 PIERCE QUANTUM FIRE ENGINE TO THE GLENDALE
  COMMUNITY COLLEGE FIRE ACADEMY

  The San Gabriel Fire Department seeks City Council approval to donate a
  surplus 2002 Pierce Quantum Fire Engine to the Glendale Community College
  Verdugo Fire Academy. The vehicle is no longer in service and has limited
  operational value for emergency response, but will provide significant training

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – August 19, 2025  5
   benefits to the academy. There is no direct fiscal impact to the City as a result
  of this donation. The engine has reached the end of its practical service life for
  San Gabriel operations, and the City avoids future maintenance, upkeep, and
  storage costs.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve the donation of the 2002
  Pierce Quantum Fire Engine to the Glendale Community College Verdugo Fire
  Academy and authorize the Fire Chief or designee to execute any required
  documents subject to final review and approval by the City Attorney to
  complete the donation.

  I. APPROVAL OF THREE-YEAR SOFTWARE LICENSE AGREEMENT WITH
  BLAZESTACK, INC. IN THE AMOUNT OF $13,241.00

  The San Gabriel Fire Department Arson Division is seeking approval for a three-
  year software license agreement with Blazestack, Inc. The software will support
  the Fire Department’s ongoing efforts to modernize operations and improve
  service delivery through a robust, cloud-based case management and report
  writing solution. The total cost of the three-year license agreement is
  $13,241.00. The fiscal impact for Fiscal Year 2025-2026 is $4,200 which is
  captured in the current budget. Future payments will be included in and
  submitted for approval in subsequent budget processes. No additional
  appropriation is necessary. The pricing per year is as follows: Year 1: $4,200,
  Year 2: $4,410, Year 3: $4,631. The three-year license will allow the City to avoid
  annual renewal fluctuations and lock in current pricing.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve the three-year software license
  agreement with Blazestack, Inc. and authorize the Fire Chief or designee to
  execute the Subscription License Agreement at attached to the Staff Report.

  J. PURCHASE OF TWO LUCAS 3 MECHANICAL CARDIOPULMONARY
  RESUSCITATION (CPR) DEVICES IN THE AMOUNT OF $76,468.11

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – August 19, 2025  6
   The Fire Department presently has one LUCAS 3 device on RA51 and is seeking
  to add an additional LUCAS 3 mechanical CPR adjunct to each fire engine,
  augmenting the inventory of life-saving equipment and enhancing service to
  the community. The cost of acquiring two LUCAS 3 CPR devices is $76,468.11,
  inclusive of all equipment, training, service plan, taxes and shipping.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council authorize the City Manager or designee
  to issue a purchase order to Stryker Sales, Limited Liability Company for two
  LUCAS CPR Devices, under a cooperative purchasing agreement and in
  compliance with the City of San Gabriel Purchasing Policy.

  K. ACCEPTANCE OF TRAFFIC RECORDS IMPROVEMENT PROJECT (TRIP)
  FUND GRANT IN THE AMOUNT OF $24,800.00

  The San Gabriel Police Department has been awarded grant funds from the
  Traffic Records Improvement Project (TRIP) in the amount of $24,800.00. The
  purpose of the TRIP Grant is to provide alternative funding sources to augment,
  but not supplant, current activities and programs. The TRIP Grant is designed
  to allocate funds towards the purchase of equipment and software for
  electronic reporting of crash data, citation reporting data and collection,
  improving the compatibility of crash and/or citation data with the state and
  national data systems, enhancing the ability to analyze trends in crashes, crash
  outcomes, and contributing factors. Fund 147 (Office of Traffic Safety Grants)
  revenue estimates for Fiscal Year 2025-2026 will be increased by $24,800.00 as
  part of the acceptance of the grant funding. Additionally, budget
  appropriations will be increased to expend the funds.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve the following:

  1. Increase estimated revenue (transfers in) and appropriation in (Account No.
  147-3229).

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – August 19, 2025  7
   2. Authorize the Police Chief to accept the Traffic Records Improvement
  Project funding to purchase the authorize item under the City’s purchasing
  policy and to administer the program according to the program’s
  guidelines.

 5. PUBLIC HEARING – None.

 6. CONTINUED BUSINESS – None.

 7. NEW BUSINESS

  A. APPEAL OF THE TRANSIENT OCCUPANCY TAX CALCULATION BY
  CHAMPION MOTEL

  Champion Motel has exercised its right to appeal the decision of the Finance
  Director’s determination of the amount of Transient Occupancy Tax (TOT) owed
  to the City for the quarters ending September 30, 2024, December 31, 2024 and
  March 31, 2025. Based on the Finance Director’s decision, the TOT liability for
  the 3 delinquent quarters is $19,107.75 – 18 of the 20 units occupied at a daily
  rate of $33.33. If Champion Motel’s contention of only 8 of 20 units occupied,
  using the same daily rate of $33.33, then the TOT liability for the 3 delinquent
  quarters will be $6,379.65, a difference of $12,728.09.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council conduct the appeal by Champion Motel
  and determine whether to uphold the Finance Director’s determination, with
  costs, modify it or grant the appeal and establish the Transient Occupancy Tax
  debt at $6,379.65.

  B. DRAFT HISTORIC RESOURCES SURVEY REPORT PHASE 2 [RESOLUTION
  NO. 25-35]

  The Draft Historic Resources Survey Report Phase 2 includes the boundary lines
  for potential Historic Districts and Planning Districts. On July 30, 2025, the
  Historic Preservation and Cultural Resource Commission considered the Draft
  Citywide Historic Resources Survey Report Phase 2 at a duly-noticed public
  hearing. The Historic Preservation and Cultural Resources Commission
  unanimously voted to recommend that the City Council adopt the Citywide

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – August 19, 2025  8
   Historic Resources Survey Report Phase 2. The Fiscal Year 2025-2026 Adopted
  Budget includes the cost for required legal publication and codification.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: This project is
  exempt from the requirements of the California Environmental Quality Act
  (CEQA) pursuant to Sections 15061(B)(3) and 15262 of the CEQA Guidelines. This
  includes a section known as the general rule and exempts projects where it can
  be seen with certainty that there is no possibility that the activity in question may
  have a significant effect on the environment.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 25-35 approving
  the Citywide Historic Resources Survey Report Phase 2.

  C. ORDINANCE NO. 721 AMENDING THE SAN GABRIEL MUNICIPAL CODE
  RELATING TO THE TRANSIENT OCCUPANCY TAX – INTRODUCTION

  This item introduces Ordinance No. 721, which makes an administrative update
  to the San Gabriel Municipal Code to reflect the increase in City’s Transient
  Occupancy Tax (TOT) rate from 10% to 12%, as approved by voters in the March
  5, 2013 election. This update is administrative in nature and ensures the
  Municipal Code aligns with the tax rate already in effect. There is no new fiscal
  impact associated with this action, as the 12% TOT rate has already been in
  effect since voter approval in 2013.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Waive full reading and introduce Ordinance No. 721 by title only:

  AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF SAN GABRIEL,
  CALIFORNIA, AMENDING SAN GABRIEL MUNICIPAL CODE SECTION 35.057
  RELATING TO THE TRANSIENT OCCUPANCY TAX

  2. Schedule the second reading and adoption for the next regular meeting of
  the City Council.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – August 19, 2025  9
   D. APPROVAL TO ENTER INTO A MULTI-YEAR CONTRACT WITH PEREGRINE,
  A SOLE-SOURCE DATA MIGRATION SYSTEM, AND AWARD A CONTRACT
  TO SUN RIDGE RIMS, INC. IN RESPONSE TO RFP NO. 25-07 [RESOLUTION
  NO. 25-34]

  The San Gabriel Police Department is seeking approval to enter into a multi-
  year lease purchase agreement with Sun Ridge, Inc. an emergency service
  Computer-Aided Dispatch and Record Management System (CAD RMS)
  platform in response to published RFP #25-07, and to enter into a multi-year
  contract with Peregrine Technologies, a sole-source law enforcement CAD/RMS
  data-integration platform. A migration/integration platform is required prior to
  implementing a new CAD/RMS system. The City will enter into a five-year
  software and equipment lease purchase agreement for the Sun Ridge Systems,
  Inc. CAD/RMS system. The total cost, financed at an interest rate of 5%, is
  $509,710, with annual payments of $101,942. At the conclusion of the five-year
  term, the City will own the software licenses and will continue to pay an annual
  support fee, which is subject to an annual increase between 2% and 6%.
  Additionally, there will be a one-time cost of $7,550 that will be added to the
  first year for an import link software for RIMS (software suite) to Crossroads
  (traffic collision, data, and report program) which includes installation and
  annual support.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Authorize the City Manager to execute a five-year Professional Services
  Agreement with Sun Ridge Systems, Inc.

  2. Authorize the City Manager to execute a three-year Professional Services
  Agreement with Peregrine.

  3. Authorize the City’s IT Department to purchase the required servers in an
  amount not to exceed $45,000.00

  4. Adopt Resolution No. 25-34 to appropriate the necessary funds for
  completion of the project.
